properties.decision:
DECIDED 2026-08-14 BY ANTHONY: **ANNOUNCE THE ABSENCE (option c)** — install what the named harness can take, and say plainly when it gets no loop trigger. Option (b), registering a real per-harness equivalent, was NOT rejected: it is compatible with this and remains available wherever an event model turns out to exist. Option (a), leaving it Claude-only and silent, is closed.

⭐⭐ AND READING `cap:nudge-path-proven` BEFORE CAPTURING CHANGED WHAT THIS REQUIRES. **The absence is ALREADY announced.** That capability is VERIFIED and its backstop reports `installed | absent | broken | unknown`, carried both on the handshake instructions — *"the one channel every session reads unasked"* — and as a machine-readable field on `loop_status`. A naive reading of "announce the absence" would have rebuilt something that exists.

🛑 **THE ACTUAL GAP IS NARROWER AND SHARPER: THE ANNOUNCEMENT CANNOT SAY WHY.** The backstop looks for a registered Stop hook. On an OpenCode or Grok project it finds none and reports `absent` — which is TRUE and reads as *"you forgot to install this"*. **It tells the user to fix something they cannot fix.** That is a different state from a Claude project where the hook was genuinely skipped, and reporting them identically sends one of the two users on an impossible errand.

⇒ SO THE REQUIREMENT IS A DISTINCTION, NOT A NEW ANNOUNCEMENT: *not installed here* (fixable — install it) versus *cannot be installed here* (permanent — the harness has no hook, so the loop is yours to run by hand). `absent` currently means both.

📌 WHY THIS FOLLOWS FROM THE PREVIOUS DECISION RATHER THAN MERELY SITTING BESIDE IT. `dec:idea-init-asks-which-harness-and-installs-only-that` (ACCEPTED, same day) makes init ASK which harness. Once the user has NAMED OpenCode, handing them silence about a missing safety net is exactly the silent-wrong-install failure that decision was taken to avoid. **Asking makes staying quiet indefensible: the moment the user tells you their harness, you owe them an honest answer about what it can and cannot have.**

🛑 A STALE CLAIM FOUND WHILE READING, AND IT IS A REAL DEFECT: `cap:nudge-path-proven`'s description ends *"This matters because reflow2_init installs no hooks at all: every consumer project has no session-end nudge, and until now nothing said so."* **That is no longer true.** `ensure_hooks` registers four events (SessionStart, two PostToolUse matchers, Stop) into `.claude/settings.local.json`, measured by running init on 2026-08-14. A VERIFIED capability is carrying a claim about a peer that changed underneath it — the description was right when written and nothing re-read it. Worth correcting on its own, and worth noting as another instance of a fact that no computation reads and therefore nothing rechecks.

═══ THE ANALYSIS THIS WAS DECIDED FROM ═══

RAISED AS BRAINSTORMING by Alex (`who:alex`), relayed by Anthony 2026-08-14 — the parenthetical half of his settings note, NOT covered by the upsert fix that closed the rest of it.

HIS WORDS: *"`reflow2 init .` should upsert `settings.local.json` **(or whatever settings file is relevant for the agent harness)** instead of replacing it."*

✅ MEASURED ON HEAD (`cbb1a19`): `ensure_hooks` writes to exactly ONE path — `project/.claude/settings.local.json`. `MCP_CONFIGS` generates three harnesses' server configs; `HOOK_EVENTS` is registered for one. **A project opened in OpenCode, Grok CLI or Copilot gets the MCP server and no loop nudge at all.**

🛑 WHY THAT IS MORE THAN AN INSTALLER ASYMMETRY: the served instructions argue for the hook in the strongest terms available — *"a discipline that depends on being remembered loses to urgency every time; fire it on a trigger, not on virtue"* — and say so because real use showed an agent under load keeps ADDING NODES while the capture→detect→ask→decide loop silently stops. Those harnesses run reflow2 with exactly the mechanism removed that exists because virtue was measured to fail.

⭐ IT COMPOUNDS WITH A SIBLING FINDING: `dec:idea-the-graph-vocabulary-never-reaches-the-user` records that reflow2 cannot observe an agent misbehaving in conversation. Here it cannot observe an agent that was never nudged either. Both are disciplines with no observer — and on a non-Claude harness there is not even a trigger.

📌 A SMALLER TELL IN THE SAME FILE: in `IGNORE_LINES`, `.mcp.json` and `.claude/settings.local.json` each carry an explanatory comment while `opencode.json` and `.vscode/mcp.json` get an empty one. The Claude path is the travelled one.

THE OPTIONS AS THEY STOOD.
(a) LEAVE IT Claude-only. **CLOSED** — after the asking decision, a named harness getting silence is indefensible.
(b) REGISTER A PER-HARNESS EQUIVALENT, same generator shape as `MCP_CONFIGS`. Not chosen now, not rejected: needs a real event model per harness, and a wrong guess produces the silently-broken hook `ensure_hooks` already refuses to create. **Ship where an event model is confirmed to exist.**
(c) ⭐ **CHOSEN** — announce the absence.
(d) MOVE THE TRIGGER OFF THE HARNESS — the server sees every tool call. Counter that keeps it unchosen: the server cannot block a session's stop, which is the one moment the nudge is worth most.

⚠️ VERSION CAVEAT: two of Alex's five notes describe defects already fixed, so he is probably on an older kit (`fact:second-user-notes-2026-08-14-two-items-already-fixed`). Measurements here are against HEAD.
properties.name: DECIDED — a harness that cannot take the loop nudge is TOLD so, and the announcement distinguishes "not installed" from "cannot be installed here"
properties.rationale: Raised under the brainstorm skill and settled the same day on Anthony's word. The capture deliberately read `cap:nudge-path-proven` in full BEFORE writing the requirement, and that read changed the answer: the announcement the decision asks for already exists, so the honest requirement is the DISTINCTION the existing announcement cannot draw rather than a second announcement beside it. Recorded that way so a later session does not build a duplicate reporter and then wonder why two things report the nudge. The stale sentence found in that capability's description is kept here as a finding rather than silently fixed, because a verified capability carrying an out-of-date claim about a peer is worth someone deciding about, not worth an agent quietly editing.
